rv.q: And so it proves with “Darling,” a poignant comic study of the bad faith and bad behavior of a narcissistic celebrity and those around him.

There’s a much better play nestling in the almost three hours of Hold On to Me Darling, but Lonergan seems unwilling to find it, leaving most of the poignancy buried between his disjointed scenes en route to a conclusion of unearned emotion.
This doomed and ridiculous bid for authenticity is at the heart of Kenneth Lonergan’s amusing and uneven Hold on to Me Darling at the Atlantic Theater Company.
But with Timothy Olyphant (Justified) anchoring a pitch-perfect cast, and with Lonergan’s absolutely uproarious script, it’s the farthest thing from tragedy.
Scene by scene, Hold On To Me Darling entertains; in its total effect, it disappoints.
It's a simple story that's drawn out at a lethargic pace, with rarely a clue of the talent or charisma Strings must have that allows people to put up with his narcissistic nonsense.
This all makes for great fun, even though there are all kinds of holes in Lonergan's plot...
It was a performance that flatlined from start to finish and nearly dragged everyone else down with it.
Just a little too heavy on the dialogue and exposition.
